STATEMENT OF ISSUES PRESENTED FOR REVIEW
1. Does a plaintiff who acquires title to property under a Sheriff's deed that has a scrivener's error obtain marketable title to the property pursuant to R.C. §5301.07 and thereby have standing to pursue claims related to the property? (Assignment of Error I)
2. Does a trial court properly grant a motion for judgment on the pleadings when the pleadings demonstrate no factual issues on the relief requested? (Assignment of Error II)
3. Does a trial court properly grant summary judgment when a plaintiff establishes that there are no genuine issues of material fact and the plaintiff is entitled to judgment as a matter of law, especially when the defendant does not respond to the motion or
vii

4. Does a trial court properly deny a motion for judgment notwithstanding the judgment and motion for new trial when the movant fails to establish any grounds for relief under Civ. R. 50 and 59? (Assignment of Error IV)
5. Is it proper for a claim for punitive damages to proceed to the jury when the jury has granted compensatory damages on claims of fraud and slander of title, and the record contains evidence on which the jury could find malice and ill will? (Assignment of Error V)

STATEMENT OF THE CASE
Appellee's Complaint was filed on July 6, 2017, requesting in part that the trial court declare that the Mechanic's Liens recorded by Appellants as Instrument Nos. 201704100047916, 201704100047917, and 201704100047918 to be void and quieting title in favor of Appellee and against Appellants. See Counts One and Four of Appellee's Complaint. R.4. Appellee's Complaint also alleged claims for slander of title and fraud. See Counts Two and Three of Appellee's Complaint. R.4.
Appellee filed a Motion for Partial Judgment on the Pleadings on August 30, 2017, requesting that the trial court grant Judgment in favor of Appellee on Counts One and Four of Appellee's Complaint. R. 35. The trial court granted Appellee's Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings on July 17, 2019, on which no appeal was filed. R. 75. The Mechanic's Liens were subsequently released of record pursuant to a subsequent Order filed on August 22, 2019, R. 88, and recorded in the Franklin County Recorder's Office on August 28, 2019.
Appellee filed a Motion for Summary Judgment on its claims and on all of Appellants' claims on April 12, 2018. R. 52. The trial court

ARGUMENT
Introduction
An appellate court review of a grant of summary judgment is de novo. Dupler v. Mansfield Journal Co., Inc., 64 Ohio St.2d 116, 413 N.E.2d 1187 (1980); Brewer v. Cleveland Bd. of Ed., 122 Ohio App.3d 378, 383, 701 N.E.2d 1023 (1997). De novo review requires that this Court review the trial court's judgments independently and without deference to it. Brown v. County Commrs., 87 Ohio App.3d 704, 622 N.E.2d 1153 (1993).
An appellate court's review of a grant of judgment on the pleadings is de novo. RotoSolutions, Inc. v. Crane Plastics Siding, LLC, 2013-Ohio-4343, I[ 13 (10th Dist.) (citing Franks v. Ohio Dept. of Rehab. & Corr., 145 Ohio App. 3d 114, 2011-Ohio-2048, I[ 5, 958 N.E. 2d 1253 (10th Dist.).
An appellate court reviews a denial of a motion notwithstanding the verdict de novo. Kenner v. Grant/Riverside Med. Care Found., 2017- Ohio-1349, I[ 22 (10th Dist.). A denial of a motion for new trial is reviewed under an abuse of discretion standard. Id.
7
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

0A443 - 188
Appellant Metropolitan has not challenged any determinations made by the jury, i.e. the jury's award or amount of compensatory damages, the jury's determination that Appellee was entitled to punitive damages and attorney's fees, or the jury's determination of the amount of punitive damages awarded. Furthermore, Appellants do not challenge the trial court's ruling on Appellants' claim of conversion, or the jury's determination that Appellants' claim of unjust enrichment was without merit.
I. APPELLEE HAD STANDING TO PURSUE ITS CLAIMS IN THE TRIAL COURT.
In its Brief, Appellant Metropolitan argues that Appellee lacked standing to proceed in the underlying matter because it lacked standing at the time Appellee filed its Complaint. Appellant Metropolitan's argument is based on the allegation that Appellee lacked marketable title at the time it filed the Complaint. Appellant Metropolitan's premise is unsupported by the facts and the law.
A party has standing to invoke the jurisdiction of the court when that party has a real interest in the subject matter of the action. State ex
8
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

0A443 - 189
rel. Dallman v. Court of Common Pleas, 35 Ohio St. 2d 176, 179 (1973). Standing is determined at the commencement of the lawsuit. Mousa v. Mount Carmel Health Sys., 2013-Ohio-2661, I 12 (10th Dist.).
R.C. §5301.07 provides as follows:
(A) As used in this section, "real property instrument" means a deed, mortgage, and installment contract, lease, memorandum of trust, power of attorney, or any instrument accepted by the county recorder under section 317.08 of the Revised Code.
(B)
(1) When a real property instrument is delivered to and accepted by the county recorder of the county in which the real property is situated, and is signed and acknowledged by a person with an interest in the real property that is described in the instrument, the instrument raises both of the following:
(a) A rebuttable presumption that the instrument conveys, encumbers, or is enforceable against the interest of the person who signed the instrument;
(b) A rebuttable presumption that the instrument is valid, enforceable, and effective as if in all respects the instrument was legally made, executed, acknowledged, and recorded.
(2) The presumptions described in division (B)(1) of this section may be rebutted by clear and convincing evidence of fraud, undue influence, duress, forgery, incompetency, or incapacity.
9
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

0A443 - 190
***
The import of R.C. §5301.07 is that the Sheriff's Deed is a valid, enforceable and effective Deed in all respects, and was so at the time it was recorded.
Many courts have held that a purchaser at a judicial sale has an interest in the property effective from the sale date. Freedom Mortgage Corp. v. Milhoan, 2014 Ohio 881; Ohio Savings Bank v. Ambrose, 56 Ohio St.3d 53 (1990); Mid-America National Bank v. Heiges, 1994 Ohio App. LEXIS 5145.
The Court, in Centr. Mortg. Co. v. Seye, 2017-Ohio-8713, I 40 (10th Dist.), held:
Under Ohio law, the acknowledgement of an instrument "is not the same as the instrument itself." Seabrooke v. Garcia, 7 Ohio App. 3d 167, 169, 7 Ohio. B. 212, 454 N.E. 2d 961 (9th Dist. 1982). The Supreme Court of Ohio has noted that the acknowledgement required by R.C. § 5301.01 "is for the purpose of affording proof of the due execution of the deed by the grantor, sufficient to authorize the register of deeds to record it." Basil v. Vincello, 50 Ohio St. 3d 185, 188, 553 N.E. 2d 602 (1990). Further, "a defectively executed conveyance of an interest in land is valid as between the parties thereto, in the absence of fraud." Id at 188-189, quoting Citizens Nat'l Bank v. Denison, 165 Ohio St. 89, 95, 133 N.E. 2d 329 (1956).
10
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

OA443 - 191
Appellee purchased the Property at issue in a Sheriff's Sale on March 31, 2017. The real property instrument - in this case, a deed - was recorded in the Franklin County Recorder's Office on May 16, 2017 as Instrument No. 201705160065349. When the Recorder's Office accepted the Deed, it created a rebuttable presumption that the instrument was valid, enforceable and effective. The law also supports that Appellee had a rebuttable presumption of an enforceable title from May 16, 2017. Appellee filed its Complaint on July 6, 2017, well after the date it acquired an interest in the real property.
Appellant Metropolitan's argument is predicated on the fact that the original notary block on the Deed states the name of the prior Franklin County Sheriff. The Sheriff's Deed had been prepared by the Cincinnati attorney for plaintiff in the foreclosure action. In fact, the notary witnessed the current Franklin County Sheriff sign the Deed, and the notary block used prior language. Upon realizing the error, Appellee (even though Appellee had nothing to do with the preparation of the Deed) obtained and filed with the Franklin County Recorder the notary's
11
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

0A443 - 192
affidavit that she witnessed the current Franklin County Sheriff sign the Deed and that the notary block misnamed the prior Sheriff.
Appellant Metropolitan cites to portions of R.C. § 5301.07 that are inapplicable to this matter. R.C. § 5301.07(C) provides that after four years, a deed does not need to be corrected for scrivener's errors. As identified in R.C. § 5301.07(C), these types of errors include an instrument not properly witnessed, a lack of certificate of acknowledgment, a defective certificate of acknowledgment, or a missing name in the granting clause where the grantor did sign the instrument.
Appellant Metropolitan asserts that the language of R.C. § 5301.07 states that a mistake in the deed requires correction if discovered within four years of recording. Appellant's proposition is not supported by the plain language of the statute. Nothing in R.C. § 5301.07 suggests that a deed is defective if that mistake is found prior to four years. In fact, the statute sets out the reverse: an instrument is effective, even with these errors, after four years.
12
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

0A443 - 193
It does not follow that a scrivener's error on the Deed creates a lack of standing to sue. Appellee acquired a real property interest when the Deed was recorded on May 16, 2017. The holding in Centr. Mortg. Co., supra, supports that the defective acknowledgement does not destroy the validity of the document itself absent a showing of fraud.
Appellant Metropolitan has not raised any argument in this Court or the trial court that the Deed resulted from fraud, undue influence, duress, forgery, incompetency, or incapacity. Nor has Appellant Metropolitan suggested that someone in the Franklin County Sheriff's Office forged the Sheriff's signature.
Appellant has not brought clear and convincing evidence under R.C. § 5301.07(B)(2) to refute the rebuttable presumption that the Deed at issue is an enforceable real property instrument. Appellant has not even suggested that the Deed is unenforceable due to fraud, undue influence, duress, forgery, incompetency, or incapacity.
Appellant essentially asks this Court to hold Appellee responsible for a mistake Appellee did not commit. Appellant asks this Court to rule against numerous cases, including Centr. Mortg. Co., supra, and hold
13
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

0A443 - 194
that recorded documents must be letter-perfect in order to be enforceable. Such a holding would upend years of law on the subject of deeds and mortgages. In short, Appellant's arguments are unsupported by fact and law and its first Assignment of Error should be denied.
II. THE TRIAL COURT PROPERLY DECIDED APPELLEE'S MOTION FOR JUDGMENT ON THE PLEADINGS.
Appellant's second assignment of error alleges that the trial court improperly decided Appellee's Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings , because Appellee lacked standing and failed to satisfy the elements of a quiet title proceeding. The trial court properly determined Appellee's Motion for Judgment on the Pleadings based on the facts and law.
Rule 12(C), Ohio Rules of Civil Procedure, provides that "[a]fter the pleadings are closed but within such time as not to delay the trial, any party may move for judgment on the pleadings." In evaluating a motion for judgment on the pleadings, a trial court "must accept material allegations in the pleadings and all reasonable inferences as true" and a movant succeeds only "if it appears beyond doubt that the [nonmovant]
14
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

0A443 - 195
cannot prove any set of facts entitling them to the requested relief." Dottore v. Vorys, 2012 Ohio Misc. LEXIS 142, 32-33.
The Ohio lis pendens statute, R.C. § 2703.26, states that:
When a complaint is filed, the action is pending so as to charge a third persons with notice of its pendency. While pending, no interest can be acquired by third persons in the subject of the action, as against the plaintiff's title.
The Court in Wheeling Corp. v. Columbus, 147 Ohio App. 3d 460, 482, 2001 Ohio 8751, 771 N.E.2d 263 (10th Dist., Franklin Co. 2001), held as follows:
While the doctrine of lis pendens does not prevent parties from transacting an interest in property subject to litigation, the doctrine does place any such conveyed interest at risk and subject to the final outcome of litigation.
Wheeling Corp. v. Columbus, supra, citing Martin, Rochford & Durr v. Lawyers Title Ins. Corp. (1993), 86 Ohio App. 3d 20, 619 N.E. 2d 1130.
The Court in Buckner v. Bank of N.Y., 2014-Ohio-568, [[29-32 (12th Dist., Clermont Co.) held as follows:
Lis pendens, which literally translates as "a pending lawsuit" is codified in R.C. 2703.26:
When a complaint is filed, the action is pending so as to charge a third person with notice of its
15
Franklin County Ohio Court of Appeals Clerk of Courts- 2021 Mar 29 3:49 PM-20AP000403

OA443 - 196
pendency. While pending, no interest can be acquired by third persons in the subject of the action, as against the plaintiff's title.
"Lis pendens prevents third parties who claim to have 'acquired an interest' in the property, after service and during the pendency of the foreclosure action, from challenging the trial court's judgment." Bates v. Postulate Invests., L.L.C., 176 Ohio App. 3d 523, 2880-Ohio-2815, I16, 892 N.E. 2d 937 (8th Dist.). While the doctrine does not prevent persons from transacting an interest in the property during the pending lawsuit, it "places any such conveyed interest at risk and notifies the parties that they 'are bound' by the decree and sale thereunder."
